posts.cooked:
We were SO close to beating Advanced Ennead last night in the Time Cataclysm. Gah it hurts to even think about it. Redeemer Fanatic, Tempest, Naturalist, and Omnitron-X managed a really good game. Everyone was up and running really well, had great draws, and got mostly help from the environment. We even made good use of Fixed Point, having Omnitron go double plating and Naturalist went Gazel/Croc. Everyone had the cards in play you wanted to have. Couldn't ask for a better hero situation.

But in the end, Shu was the last one standing. With 1 HP.

Losses like that really make you think. Everything went so well except for the winning. Maybe Naturalist (myself) shoulda went Rhino/Croc. But opening hand was Gazel heavy and Fixed Point happened to be the first environment card played. Maybe if Fanatic didn't discarded that card for Divine Focus, she would have had three cards in hand when a dead Set forced Fanatic to play her Wrathful Retribution. Maybe if Omnitron didn't timeshift out the melee/projectile plating first turn but had the Infernal plating instead, he wouldn't have lost his damage output halfway through the game.

I will beat them someday. Just gotta bring Setback and Scholar I guess.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Doing random until I get at least two new combos.

(EDIT: Dammit - I played against the wrong villain - should have been Plague Rat!  Oh well, still a decent match for the spreadsheet.)

Ennead vs. Absolute Zero - Elemental Wrath, Chrono-Ranger, and Freedom Tempest at The Block.

Ennead had Nephtwys, Atum, and Isis out - and never got reinforced.  They tossed some minor damage out, and then Atum tried tossing fire damage AZ's way while he had both modules and a Focused Apecture out.  Bad idea.

AZ got a Cold Snap out the first turn, and then rolled out modules and other equipment while using base power to run Nephtwys down.  From there it was damaging one-shots until the villains were gone.

Chrono-Ranger got Jim's Hat out right off, played By Any Means on Isis and then just pinged away.  Once Isis flipped he used Jim's Hat to move the bounty to his trash and then fished it back out.  He also played Hunter and Hunted for good effect, but also got beat up a bit due to it.

Tempest played an early Lightning Slash, then went to Grevious Hailstorm and Cleansing Downpour.  Between Hailstorm and Cold Snap the villains were losing 4 HP each per round.

The Block rolled out two agents - who targetted Isis for the most part.  They eventually went away as a Riot brought out two Time-Crazed Prisoners.  Atum dispatched them shortly later with a one-shot.

(This has only been my 2nd or 3rd game against the Ennead.  Not sure if it was a bad villain draw, a particularly good hero team against them, or whether the Ennead need advanced play to be a more serious challenge.  However, I suspect that Advanced Ennead might simply overwhelm three heroes in solo play.)

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
The Matriarch invades Megalopolis and is opposed by Argent Adept, Ra, and Young Legacy.

Game 1: Fowl, fowl, more fowl, and the damned Mask coming back three times immediately after being taken out due to Darken the Sky.  And did I mention fowl?  Perhaps a different approach is needed with these heroes?

Game 2:

Matriarch waits her first turn with two Darken the Sky plays.  Heroes roll out some cards and work on both the Matriarch and the Mask.  Adept is using Scherzo of Frost and Cold, and Ra uses a Fire Blast and Pyre to finish off the Mask.  That leaves Young Legacy opportunity to hit the Matriarch and get Motivational Charge into play.  Police Backup arrives and shoots the Matriarch as well.

Matriarch rolls out 5 fowl and a damaging one-shot.  The Adept plays an instrument, and damages the Matriarch for a few points.  Ra does Inferno to hurt the Matriarch and take out the deployed fowl.  Ra and Legacy split the retaliation damage.  Ra Pyres the Matriarch as well.  Young Legacy plays The Legacy Ring and hits Matriarch with both Motivational Charge and Atomic Glare.

The Environment plays Plummeting Monorail.  The police shoot the Matriarch.

The Matriarch plays a Carrion Field.  (So the heroes get another turn without worrying about getting hurt.)

Adept gets Young Legacy a free play - and Inspiring Presence comes out.  Scherzo of Frost and Cold nows does 4 damage.  Ra plays Imbued Fire and all the hero damage gets another +1 damage.  He Pyres the Matriarch for 4 HP as well. 

From there the heroes (and the Environment) just pound away at the Matriarch.  Cohorts come out next, but it's too late by then as the heroes just ignore them and concentrate on taking the Matriarch herself out and have enough extra sacrificial ongoing cards to handle her one-shots that destroy them.

===

However, an interesting comparison in seeing the same hero, villain, and environment combination play out completely differently in back-to-back plays.

In a fight of truly epic proportions, the Freedom Five (though Tachyon had been temporarily replaced with her alternate universe counterpart) were atatcked by a very well trained (read: Advanced) Vengeful Five in their own home!

Counting themselves incredibly lucky, every member of the Freedom Five survived the attack, but they may need some time to heal before their next encounter.

posts.name: Humble-Knight
posts.cooked:
Just beat regular Apostate with Bunker, Ra and Fanatic in Megapolis.

Apostate opened with a Pugilist, which allowed the heroes to build up a bit, Bunker got his Grenade Launcher out, Ra used his staff and Fanatic was able to draw some with Brutal Censure. The demon was dead and the sword had taken a couple hits.

Unfortunately, Hostage situation came out after that and that set the trend that the environment wanted to mess with us the whole game. The best it did for us was Close Quarters Combat and Rooftop combat , both of which helped us take down the huge amounts of relics that came out. 

Luckily, we had the orb come out early, so it really didn't affect anything too much beyond stalling us killing the sword. The Effigy came out at the same time as the first Gauntlet, which also meant the Runes came out. This was a pain because despite the massive damage Ra could do, Bunker was reduced to plinking Apostate with his GG and drawing from his Power supply, which was a good thing because the next 2 rounds there wasn't any drawing due to a traffic pileup followed by the tome. 

Bunker had a grenade Launcher, Ammo Drop, heavy plating, and Gatling Gun up most of the game. This kept his hand stocked, for Gatling Gun, but he didn't draw a turret mode, flak cannon or Omni Cannon til the last round. When the runes and the periapt were out, he sat there and twiddled his thumbs because he couldn't draw due to having a traffic pile up there 1 turn and the tome out the next. That said he did kill several relics and set Ra and Fanatic up to kill others, and tanked a good amount of damage, though whenever he was highest there was also a damage boost for Apostate, meaning he still took damage. He did avoid Gauntlet damage though.

Ra was mainly on damage duty, despite only have 1 damaging one shot. He set up fanatic to kill both the effigy and the Runes, when the heroes were not able to do much because Apostate was already at a low enough health that he could be burned through in a turn or 2. He also was on destruction fodder duty, losing a living conflagration and 2 staves. He was the one to do most of the burning through Relics dr. His Imbued Fire really powered Bunker up.

Fanatic was a bit of a jack of all trades, and often was the one to kill a tricky relic, due to being last in the order. She was always on guard with her health because she was getting hit so hard. Her sword killed both the periapt and the runes because it was able to get through the dr. She also did the second most amount of damage to Apostate due to her nemesis bonus. She also healed a bit. Ultimately, other than getting important Relic kills, she seemed a bit underwhelming. I wanted to final dive Apostate into the sword but it doesn't work so instead I just killed the sword and then chopped his head off.

Dawn is one of the few villains that the game might not be easier with. once she flips, you are sitting there getting hit by many more cards, which can really hurt. Dreamer and Miss Info are similar.

I can see how that would be the case, though in this particular instance, having an extra body on hand to beat her up worked out in my favor. It helped that two of the four Citizens drawn at game start were the fairly harmless Citizen Sweat and Citizen Autumn, both of whom can really ruin a hero’s synergy but are two of the best to get out in the first round when they can’t do anything to anyone.

So I looked at the Google sheet and noticed how few people had tackled one of my favorite villains, Skinwalker Gloomweaver. The dice decided Chrono-Ranger, Tachyon, Expatriette, and Omnitron-X would deal with him, and deal with him they did. Chrono-Ranger maladicted Gloomweaver all to heck and gone* while Tachyon did what she could when she could, Expatriette was on crowd control, and Omnitron served primarily as a damage sponge/healer who could mostly only chip at villainous HP. The venue was Freedom Tower, which was way more good for the heroes than for Gloomweaver. Probably my favorite moment of the fight was in round seven when Tachyon had zero cards in her deck and used a Lightspeed Barrage to inflict 18 points of damage on Gloomweaver, knocking him down to two for Expatriette to mercy-kill.

I’m feeling so cocky I may just go for Cosmic Omnitron next.

*I cannot bring myself to write such a horrible pun as “Hell and gone.”

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
JimB:

I’m feeling so cocky I may just go for Cosmic Omnitron next.

So here’s a lesson I learned that you might not credit me for because I apparently forgot to click the save button on my previous post an hour and change ago: do not get cocky. It pisses off Jesus or Buddha or whoever’s actually up there running the show.

It took four tries to beat Cosmic Omnitron despite a kind of dream team random roll of Legacy, Omnitron-X, Unity, and the Naturalist, and I place the blame squarely on the also randomly chosen environment Insula Primalis. When I first rolled it, I was stoked at the thought of dinosaurs taking care of drones for me, but no, all the Insula did was hurt the heroes with poison plants and volcanoes. I never got Cosmic Omnitron to half HP before a complete party wipe. At the end, I had to swallow my pride and replace the environment with the fairly toothless Mobile Defense Platform. After that, Inspiring Presence and Galvanize made sure the heroes were all doing just ridiculous amounts of damage while Omnitron-X mostly used his Rocket Punch (I’d been burned too many times to even try putting out any of those “destroy these cards if X takes damage” cards) to inflict an average of 9 points per hit, which I am totally petty enough to have taken a lot of satisfaction in. Turret Bot plugged away gamely while Unity kept throwing out Brainstorms in hopes of getting some equipment she could turn into a bot (didn’t happen), and I tried not to picture exactly how the crocodile in the corner was managing to do at least 5 points of damage to a flying spaceship-factory-thing every round.

I think having more heroes might actually work against the heroes in Omnitron’s case, because let me tell you, those Sedative Flechettes doing 5 HP to everyone frigging hurt, particularly when Unity’s bots would get wiped out by them.

posts.cooked:
Good god. Took forever, but a team of Legacy, the Wraith, Setback, and Parse took out Spite in the Final Wasteland. As usual, Legacy was MVP, using a combination of Next Evolution and Lead from the Front to first absorb the toxic damage Spite wanted to do every time someone used a power so we could damage him without trouble; then the Wraith finally got a Stun Bolt out and was able to knock his damage down by 1 so Legacy could absorb all of it harmlessly thanks to his Fortitude. Setback was there for a little bit of damage here and there, and Parse was fairly helpful early on when she was able to make damage against him irreducible or put Victim cards atop his deck (I had six under the Safe House when he finally flipped), but she didn’t have any useful cards at all in the last two round and was just crapping out Ongoing cards for the sake of sacrificing them at the start of Spite’s turn.

Really, the only thing I did that I’m actually proud of–attributing them to skill rather than luck–were my strategic choices here and there to redirect damage to Legacy so it would at least be reduced and Spite couldn’t vampirize as much of it.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: I realized I’d been handling Spite wrong this whole time and had been allowing him to vampirize damage even after he had flipped. Annoyed, I decided to try a shot again. I rolled randomly and got Legacy, Chrono-Ranger (I need to check my dice; these two are way more likely to come up than anyone else), Fanatic, and KNYFE stomped him pretty handily in the Time Cataclysm. Legacy never got out a copy of Fortitude, so I wasn’t able to use him to make the whole group passively immune to Spite’s flipped damage, but he did get out a ring, a Lead from the Front, and a Next Evolution to stop Spite from poisoning everyone any time they used a power and to buff the party continuously; plus when Spite started putting Ongoing cards back into hands, Legacy always took back Inspiring Presence so he could heal everyone each round. Chrono-Ranger kept the pressure on Spite with bounties and his Compound Bow, which quickly got frigging ridiculous. Fanatic’s base power was obviously way better than her sword, but she kept putting it out every round so it could go back to her hand every round because I am a punk like that. KNYFE did exactly what you expect KNYFE to do and put out shameful amounts of HP damage. She tanked when she could with her one shield card whose name I forget, but it really didn’t amount to much except denying Spite one extra HP of healing for a few rounds prior to flipping.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
After beating Spite like a redheaded stepchild, I thought Gloomweaver hadn’t been played against enough. The dice told me he was getting into shenanigans in the Ruins of Atlantis, so a time-traveling cowboy,* Baron Blade’s lab rat, a cyclops with mommy issues, and a janitor stapled to an Iron Man suit decided to give him what-for. What-for was given, to the surprise of no one. Krakens did a lot of the work for the heroes, honestly, but the biggest surprise was how quickly Absolute Zero got out his perpetual motion setup: in order, he got out Cold Snap, Null-Point Calibration Suit, Isothermic Transducer, Thermal Shockwave, Focused Apertures, and Cryo Chamber, so he was gaining at least 2 HP per round while picking away at all bad guys everywhere.

*I told you he’s way too likely to come up.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Citizen Dawn and RISE invade the Freedom Tower.  Opposing them is GI Bunker, Haka, and Expatriette.

See-saw fight as heroes build up equipment and then Dawn strips them away with Devastating Aura.  Citizens are generally kept in check in the early game, but an accumulation of Dawn's ongoing cards led to an accelerated run through her deck along with ressurrecting citizens out of the trash.  (The second Devastating Aura freed four citizens that Haka had accumulated under Savage Mana.  Dawn then flipped and then immediately flipped back.)

Haka was using Rampage repeatedly to keep the citizens in check, plus Ground Pound to give the heroes a bit of relief as they chipped away at Dawn's HP and kept up with her occasional heals.

The environment deck was mainly helping/hindering by putting rooms into play for a round or so, and then having them breached to add to Dawn's damage.  Which was not necessarily good for her as she had two copies of Channel the Eclipse in play and was thus inflicting extra damage on herself as well.

Last round was Dawn and some citizens incapping GI Bunker and running the other heroes down to 2-3 HP while Dawn herself was down to 2 HP.  Couldn't quite trigger GI Bunker's "destroy a 1 HP target" incap power for the win, but instead ended up giving a power use to Haka for him to do the honors.  (That Expatriette didn't go first due to nemesis damage bonus was sort of surprising.)

It's 3 in the morning and you can't get to sleep, what better thing to do than to play a 5 player game of Sentinels solo.

Fanatic, Ra, Tachyon, Tempest and the Wraith took on the mad bomber what bombs at midnight.

9 cards beneath Bomber Blade before he flipped, it wasn't helped by two-in-a-turn Hasten Dooms, followed by a Backlash Field, the heroes were really feeling the hurt. Ra felt the burn the most keeping both Solar Flares around, only for them to be destroyed because I forgot that Blade destroyed stuff when he flipped, 8 points of damage for no benefit, Guh.

Baron Blade was whittled down to 2HP and the heroes thought they had it in the bag only for him to heal himself with nanites. Backlashfield was still out and thanks to a devious disruption at the wrong time any body who hit Blade would fall in the aftermath. Heroes sacrificed themselves willingly to knock him down a peg or two until Wraith's turn when she just sat back and watched. The heroes secret backup plan of the Crushing Hallway was enough to see the Baron's plan fall flatter than the man himself, Huzzah for over-elaborate death traps!

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Dark Watch Setback came back from the future to tell Nightmist that Gloomweaver was trying to take over the Final Wasteland, which seems like kind of a wasted effort on his part but I guess whatever, your only chance to conquer the Earth is after the apocalypse when you suck as bad as he does. Going up against a god, she decided to bring a god of her own–Ra–and that god decided to bring along a weather-controlling alien because why not. About eight rounds in, the game was over because all the relics were in the trash (Setback had out his “bonk you and get some unlucky tokens” and his “eat everyone’s hits unless you spend unlucky tokens to redirect them” cards out, so he was inflicting about eleven points of damage per round), but Gloomweaver still had almost 60 HP to go, so I kept the game going just to rub his nose in it and smashed him down to nothing.

One of these days, I need to remember that Advanced Mode is a thing. It would have made this bout more interesting, at least.

posts.cooked: Omnitron flattened by Golem Unity, Bunker, Chrono-Ranger, The Sentinels, and Dark Watch Nightmist in The Final Wasteland.  Details over in Play By Forum Game #30 thread.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Cultists attempt to summon Skinwalker Gloomy in a Megalopolis cemetary.  With other heroes busy Scholar uses an experimental time device to draw GI Bunker from the past and Eternal Haka from the future to aid in defeating this menace.

Battle is joined.  Bunker ends up in Turret Mode for a while with only the Grenade Launcher going, but it's useful for damaging pins and cultists in addition to some damage to Gloomweaver himself.  Haka gets Savage Mana out early and with the help of the other heroes starts burying all the cultists, the zombies, a relic or two, and even a couple of cards from the environment deck.  The Scholar spends a lot of time early on in Energy form doing heals and damaging Gloomweaver.

Gloomweaver flips and starts doing mass damage as he manifests.  However, he does suffer from a lack of allies to draw HP from.  Bunker is still dealing out damage, but running low on HP.  Haka is still accumulating victims under Savage Mana as he also pounds on Gloomweaver.  Scholar is in Iron form to tank hitpoints and do what damage he can.

Gloomweaver is weakened, and then finished off by a 38 HP toxic blast from Savage Mana.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Took two attempts to beat Bomber Blade in Megalopolis with Redeemer Fanatic, Ra - Horus, and Scholar.

First run was the environment deck messing with the heroes.  Ra got Flesh of the Sun God out and was giving the heroes fire immunity - two turns in a row the environment put out Close Combat and converted Blade's bomb damage to melee from fire to the detriment of the heroes.  Fanatic and Ra eventually get incapacitated; with the Ra incapacitation useful for getting rid of Blade's Backlash Fields.  However, Scholar alone was not able to take Blade down, especially once Hostage Situation and Traffic Pile-Up both came out and crippled Scholar's ability to draw cards.

Second run was a much tamer environment deck.  Blade's bomb damage ramped up a little slower, and the heroes had a better card selection to use against him.  After Blade flipped it became a race to knock him down before he took out the heroes.  Fanatic played End of Days once to clear out a couple of villain ongoing cards plus a Plummeting Monorail.  Final round was Fanatic playing Sancrosanct Martyr for 5 damage, Ra playing a Fire Blast for 5 damage, and then Scholar playing Knowing When To Turn Loose and discarding his hand to finish Blade off.
